YAHOO SAYS MICROSOFT OFFER UNDERVALUES COMPANY  What was rumor this weekend 
became reality on Monday, as Yahoo said that Microsofts proposal, even at $44.6 
billion, is too small. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/11/Yahoo-says-Microsoft-offer-undervalues-company_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11
 
*Related: Robert X. Cringely asks the musical question Yahoo + Microsoft: 
What's love got to with it? Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/robertxcringely/archives/2008/02/microsoft_yahoo_2.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11
 
 
OUTFITTING THE IPHONE FOR BUSINESS  The iPhone pits security concerns, vendor 
intentions, and gadget affinities against caution-minded enterprise IT. And IT 
shops are nervous, very nervous. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/11/07NF-iphone-business_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11
 

REVIEW: APPLE'S MACBOOK AIR  Sexy. Thin. Ultraportable. Apple's MacBook Air is 
all of those, but just like the smallest machines before it, Air forces some 
practical questions of the road warrior. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/11/07TC-macbook-air_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11
 

FIVE THINGS SOA VENDORS ARE MISSING  For most SOA vendors, selling into the 
emerging marketplace doesnt seem to be going all that well, perhaps because 
they're not selling the right kind of tools. Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/realworldsoa/archives/2008/02/5_things_that_s.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11
 

LAPTOP SEARCHES AND INSECURE BORDERS  We need more secure borders, indeed. 
But how far can customs officials go in demanding access to personal electronic 
files? Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/gripeline/archives/2008/02/laptop_searches.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11


INTERNET WILL GO THE WAY OF CABLE TV  The Internet is free. Applications are free. 
The people have won! Baloney. The Internet is about as free as cable TV. Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/realitycheck/archives/2008/02/internet_will_g.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11


LIMO'S PLATFORM PICKS UP 18 PHONES  In a boon to mobile Linux, the LiMO platform 
is poised to reveal new Linux phones by major vendors. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/11/LiMo-Linux-phone-platform-picks-up-18-phones_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-11
